as="geometry"/></mxCell><mxCell id="doc-79" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=14;spacing=4;overflow=visible;" value="<ol style='margin:0;padding-left:22px'><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Building and zones</b>: single-storey office (SIA 2024 room type 3.01) in Chur, plan 30 × 15 m above an unheated basement; zone 1 = south half, zone 2 = north half (225 m² each), separated by an interior wall along the E–W axis. Roof, floor and zone areas from the outer plan dimensions, façade areas = length × storey height 3.40 m (assumption), air volume with the clear height 3.00 m.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Conduction</b> one-dimensional, constant material properties, thermal bridges neglected, window frames included in U<sub>w</sub>.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Air</b> well mixed in each zone: one air node (θ<sub>71</sub>, θ<sub>144</sub>) with C = ρcV.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Outdoor</b>: temperature source T<sub>o</sub> (weather file Chur TMYx 2004–2018) on walls, windows, roof and ventilation; h<sub>o</sub> = 25 W/(m²K) includes the long-wave exchange with sky and surroundings.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Basement</b> (unheated) as independent temperature source T<sub>bsmt</sub> = 20 °C − b (20 °C − T<sub>o,24h</sub>), b = 0.7 (assumption); surface coefficient on the basement side 1/R<sub>si,down</sub> = 5.9 W/(m²K).</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Indoor convection</b> only on the convection branches: h<sub>c</sub> = 2.5 W/(m²K) on vertical surfaces (EN ISO 6946), 3.0 W/(m²K) on ceiling and floor (assumption); long-wave radiation is modelled separately. Exception: the door has no long-wave branch and uses R<sub>si</sub> = 0.13 m²K/W (convection + long-wave) on both sides.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Indoor long-wave radiation</b> linearised at T<sub>m</sub> = 293 K, radiosity method of 03CubicBuilding; with the view factors F<sub>ij</sub> = S<sub>j</sub>/S<sub>T</sub> the network is a star (θ<sub>72</sub>, θ<sub>145</sub>) with G<sub>i</sub> = 4σT<sub>m</sub><sup>3</sup>ε<sub>i</sub>S<sub>i</sub>; ε = 0.85 opaque, 0.9 glass; surfaces in the same plane are not excluded. Reciprocity holds, the summation rule does not (Σ<sub>j≠i</sub>F<sub>ij</sub> = 1 − S<sub>i</sub>/S<sub>T</sub>, about 0.67 for roof and floor); accepted as a simplification (03CubicBuilding).</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Solar radiation</b>: Φ<sub>o</sub> = αSE on outer surfaces (α = 0.5 façade, 0.6 roof, assumption; none on the floor), Φ<sub>a</sub> absorbed in the glass, transmitted radiation distributed over the inner surfaces as Φ<sub>i</sub>; external blinds (g<sub>tot</sub> = 0.10, SIA 180: g<sub>tot</sub> ≤ 0.10) reduce the transmitted part.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Internal gains</b>: occupants, equipment and lighting with their own SIA 2024 profiles, convective; one input per air node f = Q̇<sub>occ</sub> + Q̇<sub>equip</sub> + Q̇<sub>light</sub>.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Ventilation</b> per zone: supply/exhaust with heat recovery η = 0.75 (assumption) plus infiltration as one advection branch from T<sub>o</sub>: G<sub>v</sub> = ρc[(1−η)V̇<sub>mech</sub> + V̇<sub>inf</sub>]/3600 with V̇<sub>mech</sub> = 466 m³/h (SIA 2024: 29 m³/(h·P), 14 m²/P) and V̇<sub>inf</sub> = 33.8 m³/h.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Coupling of the zones</b>: uninsulated concrete interior wall (convection, conduction, long-wave on both sides) and the closed door (U·S). No air exchange between the zones (assumption: door closed; both zones have balanced supply/exhaust, so there is no pressure difference across the door gap).</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>HVAC</b>: one P-controller per zone on the air temperature, q<sub>HVAC</sub> = K<sub>p</sub> (T<sub>sp</sub> − θ<sub>a</sub>); set-point T<sub>sp</sub> as temperature source (21 °C heating / 26 °C cooling during occupancy, SIA 2024; 18 / 28 °C otherwise, assumption); K<sub>p</sub> = 10<sup>5</sup> W/K (assumption); K<sub>p</sub> → 0 gives free running. T<sub>sp</sub> and K<sub>p</sub> are switched in time (dead band, 05SwitchModels): heating set-point when θ<sub>a</sub> &lt; T<sub>h</sub>, cooling set-point when θ<sub>a</sub> &gt; T<sub>c</sub>, K<sub>p</sub> → 0 in between.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Capacities</b> only at the mesh centres of insulation (2 meshes) and concrete (4 meshes), in the glass (glass area = 80% of the window area, frame capacity neglected) and in the air; surface nodes and θ<sub>rm</sub> without capacity.</li><li style='margin-bottom:5px'><b>Floor above the basement</b>: mineral wool 0.14 m and concrete 0.30 m in meshes; the resistances of the impact-sound insulation (EPS 0.04 m) and of the screed (0.08 m) are added to the last half mesh of the concrete (q84, q173), their capacity is neglected (assumption); U = 0.176 W/(m²K).</li></ol>" vertex="1"><mxGeometry x="3600" y="780" width="2200" height="420" as="geometry"/></mxCell><mxCell id="doc-80" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=20;fontStyle=1;" value="3 Types of walls, windows and door" vertex="1"><mxGeometry x="3600" y="1220" width="1200" height="30" as="geometry"/></mxCell><mxCell id="doc-81" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=13;overflow=visible;" value="<table style='border-collapse:collapse;font-size:13px'><tr><th style='border:1px solid #888;padding:3px 6px;background:#F2F2F2;width:240px'>Element</th><th style='border:1px solid #888;padding:3px 6px;background:#F2F2F2;width:1250px'>Layers (outside → inside), λ W/(m·K), ρ kg/m³, c J/(kg·K)</th><th style='border:1px solid #888;padding:3px 6px;background:#F2F2F2;width:110px'>U ISO W/(m²·K)</th><th style='border:1px solid #888;padding:3px 6px;background:#F2F2F2;width:130px'>U circuit W/(m²·K)</th><th style='border:1px solid #888;padding:3px 6px;background:#F2F2F2;width:300px'>Source</th></tr><tr><td style='border:1px solid #888;padding:2px 6px'>External wall</td><td style='border:1px solid #888;padding:2px 6px'>mineral wool 0.20 m (λ 0.035, ρ 30, c 1030) | concrete 0.20 m (λ 2.3, ρ 2400, c 880)</td><td style='border:1px solid #888;padding:2px 6px'>0.167</td><td style='border:1px solid #888;padding:2px 6px'>0.167</td><td style='border:1px solid #888;padding:2px 6px'>assumption (design values); All other y<sub>i</sub> = 0.<br>Input vector of the state-space model u = [b<sub>T</sub>; f<sub>Q</sub>]: the 20 non-zero entries of b in branch order, then the 28 non-zero entries of f in node order (48 inputs); state-space order = number of capacities = 72.<br>Check of A and G (steady state): all temperature sources = 1 gives θ = 1 in every node (max. deviation 1e-14); T<sub>o</sub> = T<sub>bsmt</sub> = 0 °C and T<sub>sp</sub> = 20 °C give q<sub>HVAC</sub> = 4.14 + 4.14 kW (estimate with U·A: 8.7 kW)." vertex="1"><mxGeometry x="3600" y="5261" width="2200" height="110" as="geometry"/></mxCell></root></mxGraphModel></diagram></mxfile>

div.div:
Nodes and sources
• dot with number: temperature node θ0 … θ154; dot without number: junction of wires of the same node; a crossing with a hop is not connected
• vertical wire next to the rows = star node θrm of the zone (one node, number at its top)
• number under a conductance: branch q0 … q190, arrow = assumed flow direction
• temperature sources (+ towards the node): To outdoor, Tbsmt unheated basement, Tsp,1, Tsp,2 set-points
• flow-rate sources: Φo solar absorbed by the outer surface, Φi transmitted solar absorbed by the inner surface, Φa solar absorbed by the glass (index: orientation S/N/E/W, R roof, F floor, IW interior wall, + zone)
• internal gains: one input per node, f71 = Q̇occ,1 + Q̇equip,1 + Q̇light,1 and f144 = Q̇occ,2 + Q̇equip,2 + Q̇light,2 (profiles summed)
• P-controller: qHVAC = Kp (Tsp − θa) (03CubicBuilding)
• long-wave: radiosity network of 03CubicBuilding with Fij = Sj/ST = star with Gi = 4σTm3εiSi (star-mesh theorem)
• dotted lines: layer boundaries (insulation | concrete)

text.tspan: Nodes and sources
• dot with number: temperature node θ0 … θ154; dot without number: junction of wires of the same node; a crossing with a hop is not connected
• vertical wire next to the rows = star node θrm of the zone (one node, number at its top)
• number under a conductance: branch q0 … q190, arrow = assumed flow direction
• temperature sources (+ towards the node): To outdoor, Tbsmt unheated basement, Tsp,1, Tsp,2 set-points
• flow-rate sources: Φo solar absorbed by the outer surface, Φi transmitted solar absorbed by the inner surface, Φa solar absorbed by the glass (index:
orientation S/N/E/W, R roof, F floor, IW interior wall, + zone)
• internal gains: one input per node, f71 = Q̇occ,1 + Q̇equip,1 + Q̇light,1 and f144 = Q̇occ,2 + Q̇equip,2 + Q̇light,2 (profiles summed)
• P-controller: qHVAC = Kp (Tsp − θa) (03CubicBuilding)
• long-wave: radiosity network of 03CubicBuilding with Fij = Sj/ST = star with Gi = 4σTm3εiSi (star-mesh theorem)
• dotted lines: layer boundaries (insulation | concrete)

ol.li: Building and zones: single-storey office (SIA 2024 room type 3.01) in Chur, plan 30 × 15 m above an unheated basement; zone 1 = south half, zone 2 = north half (225 m² each), separated by an interior wall along the E–W axis. Roof, floor and zone areas from the outer plan dimensions, façade areas = length × storey height 3.40 m (assumption), air volume with the clear height 3.00 m.
Conduction one-dimensional, constant material properties, thermal bridges neglected, window frames included in Uw.
Air well mixed in each zone: one air node (θ71, θ144) with C = ρcV.
Outdoor: temperature source To (weather file Chur TMYx 2004–2018) on walls, windows, roof and ventilation; ho = 25 W/(m²K) includes the long-wave exchange with sky and surroundings.
Basement (unheated) as independent temperature source Tbsmt = 20 °C − b (20 °C − To,24h), b = 0.7 (assumption); surface coefficient on the basement side 1/Rsi,down = 5.9 W/(m²K).

Indoor convection only on the convection branches: hc = 2.5 W/(m²K) on vertical surfaces (EN ISO 6946), 3.0 W/(m²K) on ceiling and floor (assumption); long-wave radiation is modelled separately. Exception: the door has no long-wave branch and uses Rsi = 0.13 m²K/W (convection + long-wave) on both sides.

Indoor long-wave radiation linearised at Tm = 293 K, radiosity method of 03CubicBuilding; with the view factors Fij = Sj/ST the network is a star (θ72, θ145) with Gi = 4σTm3εiSi; ε = 0.85 opaque, 0.9 glass; surfaces in the same plane are not excluded. Reciprocity holds, the summation rule does not (Σj≠iFij = 1 − Si/ST, about 0.67 for roof and floor); accepted as a simplification (03CubicBuilding).

Solar radiation: Φo = αSE on outer surfaces (α = 0.5 façade, 0.6 roof, assumption; none on the floor), Φa absorbed in the glass, transmitted radiation distributed over the inner surfaces as Φi; external blinds (gtot = 0.10, SIA 180: gtot ≤ 0.10) reduce the transmitted part.
Internal gains: occupants, equipment and lighting with their own SIA 2024 profiles, convective; one input per air node f = Q̇occ + Q̇equip + Q̇light.

Ventilation per zone: supply/exhaust with heat recovery η = 0.75 (assumption) plus infiltration as one advection branch from To: Gv = ρc[(1−η)V̇mech + V̇inf]/3600 with V̇mech = 466 m³/h (SIA 2024: 29 m³/(h·P), 14 m²/P) and V̇inf = 33.8 m³/h.

Coupling of the zones: uninsulated concrete interior wall (convection, conduction, long-wave on both sides) and the closed door (U·S). No air exchange between the zones (assumption: door closed; both zones have balanced supply/exhaust, so there is no pressure difference across the door gap).

HVAC: one P-controller per zone on the air temperature, qHVAC = Kp (Tsp − θa); set-point Tsp as temperature source (21 °C heating / 26 °C cooling during occupancy, SIA 2024; 18 / 28 °C otherwise, assumption); Kp = 105 W/K (assumption); Kp → 0 gives free running. Tsp and Kp are switched in time (dead band, 05SwitchModels): heating set-point when θa < Th, cooling set-point when θa > Tc, Kp → 0 in between.

Capacities only at the mesh centres of insulation (2 meshes) and concrete (4 meshes), in the glass (glass area = 80% of the window area, frame capacity neglected) and in the air; surface nodes and θrm without capacity.

Floor above the basement: mineral wool 0.14 m and concrete 0.30 m in meshes; the resistances of the impact-sound insulation (EPS 0.04 m) and of the screed (0.08 m) are added to the last half mesh of the concrete (q84, q173), their capacity is neglected (assumption); U = 0.176 W/(m²K).

Roof, floor and zone areas from the outer plan dimensions, façade areas = length × storey height 3.40 m (assumption), air

div.div: C θ̇ = −ATGAθ + ATGb + f, q = G(−Aθ + b) (03CubicBuilding). A has 191 rows (branches q) and 155 columns (nodes θ): −1 where qk leaves a node, +1 where it enters; a branch that starts at a temperature source has only the +1. As in 04AssemblingCircuits the matrices are assembled from the element circuits on the right; G = diag(G0 … G190) and C = diag(C0 … C154) hold the values of tables 6 and 7.

text.tspan: C θ̇ = −ATGAθ + ATGb + f, q = G(−Aθ + b) (03CubicBuilding). diag(C0 … C154) hold the values of tables 6 and 7.

div.div:
y (155 entries): outputs are the air temperatures, y71 = y144 = 1 (θ71 zone 1, θ144 zone 2); for the operative temperature also θ72, θ145. All other yi = 0.
Input vector of the state-space model u = [bT; fQ]: the 20 non-zero entries of b in branch order, then the 28 non-zero entries of f in node order (48 inputs); state-space order = number of capacities = 72.
Check of A and G (steady state): all temperature sources = 1 gives θ = 1 in every node (max. deviation 1e-14); To = Tbsmt = 0 °C and Tsp = 20 °C give qHVAC = 4.14 + 4.14 kW (estimate with U·A: 8.7 kW).
